meta.title: Dolgate — open-source SSH workspace
meta.description: An open-source SSH workspace for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android. Terminal, SFTP, port forwarding and tmux in one app, with hosts, keys and snippets synced end-to-end encrypted. Self-hostable sync server.
meta.ogDescription: An open-source SSH workspace that carries on from desktop to mobile

runtime.dlAppStore: Get it on the App Store

keys.hero.h1:
An open-source SSH workspace,
from desktop to mobile without a break.
keys.hero.sub: Plain SSH, EC2 SSM, tmux, SFTP and port forwarding in one app. Hosts, keys and snippets sync end-to-end encrypted — and you can run the sync server yourself.
keys.feat.h2: Everything a terminal needs, in one app
keys.feat.sub: From plain SSH to AWS SSM, containers and tmux — the whole of server work in a single workspace.
keys.card.ssh.d: Plain SSH, EC2 SSH-over-SSM, SSM shell fallback, ECS Exec, SFTP and port forwarding in one app. SSH agent auth and agent forwarding included.
keys.card.tmux.d: Remote tmux windows become app tabs and panes become split views. Closing a tab detaches instead of killing, so the session survives and picks up where you left off.
keys.card.ai.d: Ask about the current session using its host details and terminal output. Read-only commands run on their own; anything that changes state waits for your approval. Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs, Claude and Codex.
keys.card.record.d: Replay a finished terminal session on a timeline. Recordings stay on the device and are never uploaded.
keys.card.sync.d: Hosts, secrets and snippets sync between desktop and mobile with end-to-end encryption. The sync server (sync-api) runs from a single Docker command if you want to host it yourself.
keys.card.tailnet.d: The app itself joins as a tailnet node. It reaches hosts inside a tailnet with no Tailscale client and no VPN permission, and never touches your OS routing or DNS.
keys.net.h2: See your port forwards and tunnels
keys.net.sub: Local, remote and dynamic forwards, SSM forwards and container tunnels all live in one list. For connections through a jump host, point ProxyJump at a saved host and you are done.
keys.sec.h2: Somewhere you can leave your passwords and keys
keys.sec.sub: Secret handling is the baseline for an SSH client. The rule here is simple — no secret is ever left in plaintext. The design is public in the data protection document.
keys.sec.item1.t: Stored only in the OS secure store
keys.sec.item1.d: Passwords, private keys and API keys are encrypted through macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI, iOS Keychain or Android Keystore. With no secure store available, saving is refused rather than falling back to plaintext.
keys.sec.item2.d: Sync data is encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM before upload, and the encryption key opens only with the sync passphrase you set. Managed or self-hosted, the operator cannot decrypt it.
keys.sec.item3.d: Terminal output, session recordings, activity logs and AI API keys never leave the device.
keys.sec.item4.d: The whole codebase is public so you can verify it yourself, and the sync server can run on your own infrastructure.
keys.self.sub: The sync-api that handles browser sign-in and sync is a single container. Start it, then point the app at your address from its sign-in screen.
keys.self.note: See the self-hosting guide for the full configuration.
keys.dl.sub: Every platform ships on the same version, and desktop builds update themselves.
keys.dl.note: Linux ships .deb and .rpm for x86_64 and arm64. Pick one from ▾ on the button above, or see the full list on the releases page.
